item.title: Contact
item.description:
I welcome discussions and collaborations related to structural health monitoring, digital twins, scientific machine learning, scientific computing, and intelligent infrastructure systems.

Assistant Professor
Department of Civil Engineering
Indian Institute of Technology Bombay
Mumbai, India

Research Areas
#

  • Structural Health Monitoring
  • Digital Twins
  • Physics-Informed Machine Learning
  • Scientific Computing
  • Computer Vision
  • Intelligent Infrastructure Systems

Collaboration and Student Enquiries
#

Prospective students, researchers, and collaborators are encouraged to contact regarding:

item.title: Uncertainty Quantification
item.description:
Uncertainty quantification focuses on understanding, modelling, and propagating uncertainty in sensing, modelling, prediction, and decision-making for civil infrastructure systems.

This theme is suitable for students interested in reliability, Bayesian inference, probabilistic modelling, digital twins, structural health monitoring, and risk-informed infrastructure decisions.

Project Directions
#

Uncertainty-Aware Structural Health Monitoring
#

Develop methods to quantify uncertainty in damage detection, localization, and condition assessment of infrastructure systems.

item.title: Openings
item.description:
I am actively looking for motivated PhD and M.Tech students interested in mechanics-informed AI, structural health monitoring, digital twins, scientific machine learning, computer vision, sensing technologies, and AI-assisted infrastructure monitoring.

PhD students are expected to pursue long-term research directions, while M.Tech students can take up focused thesis problems with clear research objectives and potential for strong technical contributions. Motivated B.Tech students interested in early research exposure are also encouraged to connect.

item.title: System Identification
item.description:
System identification focuses on learning mathematical and computational models of engineering systems from measured data. In structural engineering, this is central to understanding dynamic behaviour, detecting changes, and building reliable digital twins.

This theme is suitable for students interested in structural dynamics, nonlinear systems, signal processing, Kalman filtering, sparse regression, and interpretable machine learning.

Project Directions
#

Identification of Nonlinear Dynamical Systems
#

Develop methods to identify interpretable models of nonlinear structural systems from noisy and limited measurements.

item.title: Drone-Based Monitoring
item.description:
Drone-based monitoring uses unmanned aerial platforms, cameras, and non-contact sensing methods for inspection, measurement, and monitoring of civil infrastructure systems.

This theme is suitable for students interested in computer vision, infrastructure inspection, vibration measurement, sensing systems, robotics-assisted monitoring, and field-oriented structural health monitoring.

Project Directions
#

Drone-Assisted Infrastructure Inspection
#

Develop drone-based workflows for visual inspection of bridges, buildings, and other civil infrastructure systems.

item.title: Teaching
item.description:
Teaching is focused on developing strong fundamentals in mechanics, structural engineering, numerical methods, and scientific computing while connecting them with modern computational and data-driven approaches.

Courses
#

Finite Element Method
#

Fundamentals of finite element formulations, weak forms, interpolation functions, isoparametric elements, numerical integration, and applications to structural and continuum mechanics.

item.title: Scientific Computing
item.description:
Scientific computing provides the computational foundation for modelling, simulating, identifying, and interpreting engineering systems. In this research theme, numerical methods, mechanics, and machine learning are combined to develop reliable computational tools for civil and structural engineering.

This theme is suitable for students interested in finite element methods, numerical modelling, inverse problems, PDEs, scientific machine learning, and computational mechanics.

Project Directions
#

Scientific Machine Learning for Engineering Problems
#

Develop computational methods that combine numerical simulation, governing equations, and machine learning for engineering applications.

item.title: Computer Vision for Infrastructure
item.description:
Computer vision for infrastructure monitoring uses images and videos to measure, inspect, and interpret the behaviour and condition of civil infrastructure systems.

This theme is suitable for students interested in image processing, video-based measurement, deep learning, structural dynamics, and AI-assisted infrastructure inspection.

Project Directions
#

Vision-Based Displacement and Vibration Measurement
#

Develop image/video-based methods to estimate displacement, vibration response, and dynamic properties of structural systems.

item.title: Research
item.description:
My research focuses on mechanics-informed intelligent systems for monitoring, modelling, and decision-making in civil infrastructure.

The work is organized around the following research themes. Each theme connects to possible student projects, graduate research directions, and collaborative opportunities.

Structural Health Monitoring

Vibration-based and data-driven methods for damage detection, localization, and condition assessment of civil infrastructure.

View projects →

Digital Twins

Mechanics-informed digital twins that combine sensing data, computational models, and AI for infrastructure state estimation.

item.title: About
item.description:
Prof. Ashish Pal is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Civil Engineering at the Indian Institute of Technology Bombay. His research lies at the intersection of structural engineering, scientific computing, sensing technologies, and artificial intelligence.

His work focuses on developing mechanics-informed intelligent systems for structural health monitoring, digital twins, scientific machine learning, and resilient infrastructure monitoring.

Research Vision
#

The long-term goal of the research is to develop intelligent infrastructure systems capable of autonomous sensing, interpretation, prediction, and decision support through the integration of mechanics, sensing technologies, data, and machine intelligence.

item.title: Physics-Informed Machine Learning
item.description:
Physics-informed machine learning integrates governing equations, mechanics, numerical methods, and data-driven models to develop interpretable and reliable computational tools for engineering systems.

This theme is suitable for students interested in scientific machine learning, structural dynamics, PDEs, inverse problems, and mechanics-guided artificial intelligence.

Project Directions
#

Physics-Informed Learning for Structural Dynamics
#

Develop machine learning models constrained by equations of motion for predicting and identifying structural dynamic response.

item.title: Digital Twins for Civil Infrastructure
item.description:
Digital twins for civil infrastructure combine mechanics-based models, sensing data, state estimation, and machine learning to enable real-time monitoring, prediction, and decision support.

This theme is suitable for students interested in structural dynamics, finite element modelling, sensing, system identification, uncertainty quantification, and AI-assisted infrastructure management.

Project Directions
#

Digital Twin of an RC Bridge or Building Frame
#

Develop a computational digital twin that combines finite element modelling, vibration data, and state estimation for monitoring structural condition.

item.title: Structural Health Monitoring
item.description:
Structural health monitoring focuses on sensing, interpreting, and assessing the condition of civil infrastructure systems such as bridges, buildings, and structural components.

This theme is suitable for students interested in structural dynamics, vibration-based damage detection, sensing, signal processing, machine learning, and infrastructure condition assessment.

Project Directions
#

Vibration-Based Damage Detection
#

Develop methods to detect and localize damage using measured vibration response, modal properties, and data-driven indicators.
